differential: Periorbital cellulitis
Unilateral periorbital swelling in a child suggests possible infection.
Allergic reaction
Periorbital swelling can be a manifestation of an allergic response.
Nephrotic syndrome
This can present with periorbital edema due to protein loss.
Viral conjunctivitis
Viral infections can cause periorbital swelling, especially in children.
Insect bite
An insect bite near the eye could cause localized swelling.
Nephrotic syndrome
The periorbital and lower extremity edema, along with the patient's age, strongly suggest nephrotic syndrome as a likely cause.
Glomerulonephritis
Edema and age could indicate a glomerulonephritis, although the unremarkable exam makes this less likely than nephrotic syndrome.
Heart failure
While less likely given the age and lack of respiratory symptoms, heart failure could present with edema.
Protein-losing enteropathy
This condition can cause edema due to hypoalbuminemia, although it is less common than nephrotic syndrome in this age group.
Allergic reaction
Although less likely with the persistent edema, an allergic reaction could cause periorbital edema, but would not explain the lower extremity edema as well.
Nephrotic syndrome
The presence of periorbital and lower extremity edema, 4+ proteinuria, elevated protein/creatinine ratio, hypoalbuminemia, and fatty casts strongly suggests nephrotic syndrome.
Minimal change disease
This is the most common cause of nephrotic syndrome in children, presenting with edema, proteinuria, and normal complement levels.
Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis
This is another potential cause of nephrotic syndrome, although less common than minimal change disease in young children, and can present with similar findings.
Membranous nephropathy
While less common in children, membranous nephropathy can cause nephrotic syndrome, presenting with proteinuria and edema.
Membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis
Although complement levels are normal, early stages or certain types of MPGN could present with nephrotic syndrome before complement abnormalities are fully established.
